name: Authenticity & Counterfeit Doubt
mechanism: A specific, recurring belief or fear that a product is fake/counterfeit, present as a pre-purchase barrier (doubt blocks the decision), a post-purchase confirmation (received item believed fake), and as an explicitly cited reason for abandoning the platform.

name: Return & Refund Process Friction
mechanism: The return/refund process itself (not the reason for returning, the process of getting money or a replacement back) is confusing, slow, or perceived as designed to fail. The single largest theme in the corpus by volume.

name: Trust Collapse → Stated Refusal to Repurchase
mechanism: Cause-agnostic: cumulative negative experience (of any kind, not authenticity-specific) crossing a threshold and manifesting as an explicit statement of reduced or eliminated willingness to buy again, including polarized for/against trust declarations and competitive switching language.

name: Delivery & Fulfillment Reliability
mechanism: Whether the order arrives at all, on time, and matching what was ordered: logistics and on-arrival quality/fit mismatch, distinct from authenticity suspicion (T1) and from the resolution process afterward (T2).

name: Cross-Platform Comparison Shopping
mechanism: User pauses the Myntra decision to actively benchmark against Amazon/AJIO/Meesho/Flipkart/Nykaa/offline on price, quality, or trust before deciding. The comparison dimension varies; the behavior (external benchmarking as a decision-stalling step) is the same mechanism throughout.

name: Missing Product Information Blocks Decision
mechanism: Specific, nameable product-attribute or policy information (fabric, safety/certification, return terms) is absent or ambiguous, stalling the move from wishlist to purchase, distinct from sizing specifically (T11) and from authenticity doubt (T1).

name: Wishlist as a Deliberate Price-Tracking Tool
mechanism: The wishlist is being used as intended by a meaningful share of savers: a deferred-purchase mechanism gated on a future price drop or sale event, not a bookmark or bug.

name: External Discovery → Purchase-Access Friction
mechanism: User discovers a product via external social/video content and wants a direct path to save or buy it; the gap between seeing it and being able to act on it inside the app is the friction. Carries a labeling-precision caveat: several members are literally 'please share the link' comments, not classic wishlist-save reasoning.

name: Price & Timing-Driven Deferral
mechanism: Purchase intent already exists; budget cycle, sale-event timing, or seasonal relevance is the stated reason for delaying, not an unresolved product doubt.

name: Operational Barriers at the Final Purchase Step
mechanism: The user is ready to buy and is blocked by the platform's own systems at the last step: payment/checkout technical failures and inventory/size unavailability are different proximate causes but share the same functional role, an operational obstruction after intent is already formed.

name: Sizing & Fit Confidence Gap (pre-purchase)
mechanism: Specifically sizing (mapping a body measurement to a size label) as an unresolved pre-purchase question, distinct from general product-quality doubt (T6) and from fit/fabric letdown after receipt (part of T4).

name: External Social Validation & Discovery-Seeking
mechanism: Seeking influencer/peer social proof or brand discovery before trusting Myntra's own product page, distinct from T5's retailer-vs-retailer price/product comparison; this is about the source and credibility of information, not competitive benchmarking.
